items.title: Adversarial artificial intelligence
items.author: William Mitchell Reid
items.summary: As military AI use grows, attacks that disrupt or deny AI systems could threaten strategic stability. This study examines risks to military and critical infrastructure systems, and recommends measures to reduce attacks and their impact globally.
items.body:
Implications of strategic stability attacks on military AI systems

ResearchPublished Sep 29, 2026

This research was sponsored by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO).

Strategic competition in military AI is intensifying, but governance has not kept pace. As reliance on AI-enabled decision making grows, adversarial attacks that disrupt, deny or manipulate military and critical infrastructure systems could undermine strategic stability. This study examines how such attacks may affect credibility, escalation, trust and attribution, and recommends measures to reduce their likelihood and impact worldwide.

Strategic competition in artificial intelligence (AI), including in the military domain, is intensifying, while global governance has not kept pace. The tactical implications of military AI are well documented: autonomous targeting, navigation in robotic systems, and decision-support tools for commanders are relatively well understood. Growing attention is now directed toward AI’s strategic effects and its influence on strategic stability.

Although research on the strategic implications of AI and governance options is expanding, it largely focuses on the potential benefits of effective AI systems. Little attention has been paid to how the disruption or denial of AI systems could threaten strategic stability. As a result, governance proposals rarely address these risks. Yet as AI is increasingly integrated in decision making and reliance on these systems grows, the consequences of adversarial interference will likewise intensify.

This project, commissioned by the UK Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), offers insights into how adversarial AI attacks targeting AI systems integrated in the military or critical national infrastructure may affect strategic stability, and offers recommendations to decrease the probability and impact of adversarial attacks on AI systems.

- The (perceived) vulnerability of AI systems to adversarial attacks undermines the credibility of defence to adversaries and allies.

- Adversarial AI may tip the offence-defence balance in favour of the offence.

- Ambiguity, distinguishing ‘normal’ AI malfunction due to model fragility and deliberate adversarial attacks, and the difficulty of attribution create opportunities for miscalculation and mistrust. Empowerment of non-state actors through democratisation of technology, and specifically adversarial AI, further complicates attribution.

- Entanglement of conventional and nuclear C3 increases the risk of an accidental attack on NC3, risking escalation.

- Governments should treat adversarial AI as a strategic stability risk, not merely a cyber security or AI assurance issue. They should incorporate these risks into national governance and international forums; share threat information with allies, incidents, attribution and emerging techniques; review significant incidents; and develop expertise across foreign policy, defence, security, cyber and assurance communities. They should strengthen AI-enabled military systems, nuclear and dual-use command, control and communications, and critical infrastructure through robust design, resilience, recovery planning and fallback options. Clear red lines, response options and communication channels with competitors are also needed to reduce miscalculation, mistrust and escalation risks.

items.title: Evaluating the UK Government’s 10-year drug strategy
items.author: Carol Black
items.summary: Dame Carol Black, Lucy Strang, and Jennifer Newbould discuss RAND Europe’s evaluation of the first three years of implementation of the Treatment and Recovery Portfolio as part of the UK government’s 10-year drug strategy, From Harm to Hope.
items.body:
D-SITAR Methods Report

Apr 22, 2026

The captions for this video are auto-generated and have not been edited.

VideoPublished Sep 28, 2026

Dame Carol Black, Lucy Strang, and Jennifer Newbould discuss RAND Europe’s evaluation of the first three years of implementation of the Treatment and Recovery Portfolio as part of the UK government’s 10-year drug strategy. While the funding has been a welcome boost and there is wide support for the Portfolio’s aims, it has not yet achieved a world-class treatment system and a whole-system approach to alcohol and/or other drugs.

Dame Carol Black

It seems to me it's extremely important - I know there are lots of other very, very important things going on - but if you want better health and you want a safer society, you need to pay attention to drugs.

In 2021, drug-related deaths in the UK were the highest ever recorded. Dame Carol Black's independent review of drugs found that drugs cost an estimated £19bn to society annually and that long-term cuts in funding have led to a decline in skills, expertise and capacity in the treatment and recovery system.

My review of drugs was commissioned by the then Home Secretary who was Sajid Javid and he asked me to do it in two parts. The first part was to really look at the evidence of where we were with the drug scene and with addiction. Wherever you looked, it didn't matter which part of the drug agenda you looked at, we were in a bad place.

In response to the issue, the UK government published their 10-year drug strategy From Harm to Hope. This strategy included an additional £780m in funding over three years for the treatment and recovery system.

So over the past two-and-a-half years, RAND Europe and our partners have evaluated the first three years of the drug strategy's Treatment and Recovery Portfolio implementation in England. We evaluated the Portfolio as a whole, as well as focusing in on five priority areas which are the housing support grant, efforts to improve the treatment and recovery workforce, lived-experience recovery organisations, the integration of mental and physical health services and the provision of depot buprenorphine, which is a long-lasting medication used for opioid substitution therapy in the recovery process. So the workforce within the treatment and recovery sector was obviously a key priority of this additional investment. There was a widespread recognition that, after years of disinvestment, the state of the workforce had been depleted and it was a real challenge to build that up over time, specifically within the planned timelines of the Portfolio.

Our findings suggest that it's not necessarily the nature of the work that leads people to leave the sector, but other factors such as salary levels, job security, workload and the availability of resources. All these things are amenable to change and are what ultimately affect people's desire to continue in the treatment and recovery sector.

Another key priority of the Treatment and Recovery Portfolio was to improve mental and physical health service integration. So it's really critical for people who use treatment and recovery services to also have really well-integrated support from both mental and physical health services. This is because a lot of their needs are also extending to other mental health challenges or physical health needs and we do find that these individuals can often fall through the cracks between these services.

So we've now got three more years of money. And if I had to concentrate now it would be on absolutely addressing the quality issue: the quality of the workforce, the quality of what is done in the treatment areas really being more sophisticated and person-centred about delivery.

What we found through our evaluations was a few really important steps that the government should take in ensuring that the Treatment and Recovery Portfolio meets its intended aims and continues to provide really good outcomes for people who are using these services and for people who are working in the sector. First of all, we recommended that the government continue to provide more funding security to really ensure that the full 10 years of the Portfolio will be recognised and realised.

So the funding was well received, but in many areas people felt that it just replaced years of disinvestment. If we don't invest in people who use drugs and alcohol now, the problem will only get larger in the future.

We also really emphasised the importance of continuing to make progress with mental and physical health service integration to ensure that people who are using these services have all their needs addressed in a really collaborative and cohesive way.

We have failed so far to get drug addiction considered a chronic health condition and given the parity of a health condition. We haven't succeeded to improve the physical complications that drug-dependent people suffer from.

We also found that there is more work to be done in ensuring a whole-system approach to dealing with drug issues. So that involves work and collaboration across multiple sectors including health, education, employment, criminal justice and so on.

I would say please empower your local delivery services to be brave, to be less bureaucratic and to deliver a person-centred service. These are individuals with complex problems and they needed not to be treated as a number, a form-filling exercise. They need to be treated as a person with a chronic health condition, given some choice and able to go along a journey which will lead to recovery.

items.title: Ministry of Defence Police: misconduct hearings
items.summary: Find out about misconduct hearings involving Ministry of Defence Police (MDP) officers and how to attend these public hearings.
items.body:
To increase openness and transparency in the MDP (and the police service in general), misconduct hearings, special case hearings and police appeals tribunals, involving Police Officers, are held in public.

Misconduct hearings deal with allegations of gross misconduct committed by MDP officers on or off duty. Gross misconduct is defined as ‘a breach of the police standards of professional behaviour ( PSPB )’ that is so serious as to justify dismissal’. Misconduct hearings form part of the disciplinary process and are not criminal proceedings.

Accelerated Misconduct Hearings

Accelerated Misconduct Hearings take place when the investigation of allegations of Gross Misconduct, committed by MDP officers on or off duty, identifies that special conditions, such as the following are satisfied:

that there is sufficient evidence, in the form of written statements or other documents, to establish on the balance of probabilities that the conduct of the officer concerned constitutes Gross Misconduct

it is in the public interest for the officer concerned to cease to be a member of the MDP without delay

Police Appeals Tribunals

Police Appeals Tribunals deal with appeals submitted by MDP officers, against the findings and/or the outcomes of misconduct hearings (including accelerated misconduct hearings), under the MDP Conduct Regulations, or stage 3 meetings under the Performance Regulations.

The decision to hold misconduct hearings and police appeals tribunals in public was announced by the Home Secretary in 2015. The Ministry of Defence Police followed suit in March 2017 by amendments to the Ministry of Defence Police conduct (2015) and performance (2012) regulations, and by subsequent revision of those Regulations into the new Ministry of Defence Police (Conduct, Performance and Appeals Tribunals) Regulations 2020, which came into effect for all cases assessed as Gross Misconduct after 2 November 2020.

This change of legislation does not affect misconduct meetings, where a breach of PSPB does not amount to gross misconduct. These proceedings will be held in private and the public have no right to observe (except in the case of a complainant or the commission^, where appropriate).

^Director General (IOPC) or Ombudsman (NI) if they conducted or directed the investigation.

What happens at a misconduct hearing

At a misconduct hearing the facts are heard by a panel, often with the help of witnesses, to enable a finding to be made. If an officer is found to have committed misconduct or gross misconduct, depending on the circumstances, the available outcomes are:

written warning (only if misconduct only found)

final written warning

reduction in rank

dismissal without notice

What happens at an Accelerated Misconduct Hearing

An accelerated hearing is heard by the Chief Constable. Due to the evidence being incontrovertible there is no requirement for any witness attendance. If an officer is found to have committed gross misconduct, the available outcomes are:

What happens at a Police Appeals Tribunal

Police appeals tribunals are heard by a panel chaired by a person nominated by the Lord Chancellor who satisfies the judicial appointment criteria. The tribunal determines whether the ‘grounds of appeal’ on which the appellant relies, have been made out. On the determination of an appeal, a tribunal may make an order dealing with the appellant in any way in which they could have been dealt with at the original hearing.

Attending a misconduct hearing

Any member of the public or press can request to attend a misconduct hearing, provided that they are aged 18 or over.

When the date of a misconduct hearing is confirmed, the details will be published below. Due to the MDP being a national force the location of the misconduct hearing may vary (dependent upon the case).

Please note the following conditions of entry:

any member of the public or press wishing to attend must register in advance, by the specified closing date, and using the MDP misconduct hearing registration form ( PDF , 178 KB , 2 pages ) they must also provide valid photo identification (for example passport or driving licence) upon attendance. (To fill out the misconduct hearing form on a mobile device you must make sure that the PDF is opened in the editable mode.)

any person who is a witness at the proceedings will not be permitted to attend prior to giving their evidence but, may be permitted to take a seat in the public gallery after this time

priority will be given to interested parties and attendance will then be granted on a ‘first come, first served’ basis (up to the capacity of the venue)

any restrictions on reporting will be notified in advance of the hearing

members of the public and press are to remain silent at all times while the hearing is in session

no photographs, film or sound recording are permitted; mobile phones and other devices can be retained but must be switched off during the hearing

any conditions particular to an individual hearing will be published on this page in advance of the hearing

where a hearing is adjourned for an extended period, attendees may be expected to leave the premises and return at the appointed time; if the hearing is held within an MOD establishment members of the public and press will be escorted from the gate to the venue and back; they will not be permitted to leave the venue except to leave the establishment

no food or refreshments, with the exclusion of water, will be permitted in the hearing room; however, an area will be set aside for use by members of the public when the panel adjourn for short periods of time

no refreshments will be provided by the MDP and if held at an MOD establishment, there may be no facilities to purchase food; in this instance, attendees should be self sufficient

we cannot reimburse any expenses you incur by attending and please note that in some cases a hearing may be cancelled at short notice; in these situations, we will do our best to notify you but, it may not be possible

members of the public and press, together with any bags, will be subject to a security search as a condition of entry and exit; anything that can be used or adapted to cause injury or damage will not be permitted

If you require disabled access, or have any other reasonable adjustment requirements, please advise us of your requirements on your registration form.

Once all applications to attend have been received and reviewed (after the closing date), your attendance will be confirmed, as applicable, by the means identified on your registration form.

Please note: in exceptional circumstances, the Chair can exclude anyone from all or part of the hearing at his/her discretion and may impose conditions relating to the attendance of any person.

Should the Secretary of State for Defence consider it expedient in the interests of national security, he/she may also give direction that:

all or part of the hearing must be conducted in private

a specified person must be excluded from all or part of the hearing

specific steps are taken to conceal the identity of a witness

specific information must be excluded from the published notification of misconduct hearings or notification of outcome

If a decision is made to hold a hearing in private the reasons will be published below and, where conditions are placed on any person’s attendance, that person will be notified prior to commencement of the hearing.

Subject Officer: PC Murray

Hearing date: 30 September 2026

Alleged Conduct (& PSPBs breached):

It is alleged that on eight occasions between May and December 2024 the Officer made expense claims for £699.88 while on rest days and/or on leave. It is alleged that this was in contravention of the MOD Travel and Subsistence Policy.

It is alleged that the Officer has breached the following standards of professional behaviour:

honesty and integrity

orders and instructions

duties and responsibilities

Members of the press or public wishing to attend the Misconduct Hearing must register to do so. Anyone who has not pre-registered will not be allowed to access the hearing. Those attending are not allowed to record or film the proceedings.

Members of the media and public may attend subject to the following conditions:

the taking of photographs and the use of film or sound recording equipment during the hearing, except for official use, is prohibited

any accredited member of the media attending the hearing by the video conference link must produce valid identification if required to do so

there may be parts of the hearing which are held in private session; if that is the case, any accredited member of the media or public attending the hearing will be asked to leave during the private session, and will be informed by the Hearings Officer when they can return

To register, email MDP -PSD-GMB@mod.gov.uk with the following details:

contact telephone number

your email address

All requests to attend must be received on or before 28 September 2026

Subject Officer: PC Fergusson

Hearing date: 21 – 25 September 2026

PC Fergusson will answer allegations that she breached the Standards of Professional Behaviour set out in Schedule 3 to the Ministry of Defence Police (Conduct, Performance and Appeals Tribunals) Regulations 2020.

It is alleged that:

while on detached duty to the Ministry of Defence Police’s Professional Standards Department (PSD), PC Fergusson accessed the PSD computer system to access cases concerning other officers without having a legitimate policing purpose to do so

PC Fergusson breached the Standards of ‘Orders and Instructions’, ‘Duties and Responsibilities’, ‘Confidentiality’, and ‘Discreditable Conduct’

PC Fergusson’s conduct, if proven, amounts to gross misconduct or, in the alternative, misconduct

All requests to attend must be received on or before 14 September 2026.

Upcoming police appeals tribunals

There are currently no upcoming police tribunals.

Previous hearings and outcomes

Subject Officer: FPS Kay

Hearing date: 1 September 2026

Alleged Conduct (and PSPBs breached):

It is alleged that former PS David Kay breached the following standards of professional behaviour:

Honesty and Integrity

It is alleged that the officer breached the standards of professional behaviour by, whilst still serving in the MDP , misrepresenting that he was not a serving member of the force on LinkedIn, in order to benefit his personal electrical company.

It is alleged that this conduct, if proved, amounts to gross misconduct.

Finding : Gross Misconduct

Outcome : Dismissed without notice if still serving

items.summary: This study develops a game-theoretic model to explain why jihadist expansion has strained traditional Western partnerships and encouraged governments to seek Russian assistance.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: Defence and Peace Economics, Volume 37, Issue 6, pages 960-980 (2026). DOI: 10.1080/10242694.2026.2687488

The Sahel has become the epicenter of global terrorism, accounting for half of all terrorism-related fatalities by 2024. Jihadist groups pursuing system-transforming agendas have expanded across the region by aligning with local militant actors and building durable insurgencies. Their growth has disrupted longstanding security relationships between Sahelian governments and France, the United States, and the United Kingdom, with many of these new states reorienting and seeking security support from Russia. This study develops a game-theoretic model to explain why jihadist expansion has strained traditional Western partnerships and encouraged governments to seek Russian assistance. We also present an alternative model demonstrating how negotiated settlements can reduce jihadist appeal and limit external rival influence. We show that jihadist groups enhance local militants’ capabilities, reducing prospects for negotiated settlements with host states. At the same time, jihadist intervention increases the political and military costs borne by Western partners, weakening their capacity to sustain long-term security commitments. These dynamics create opportunities for Russia to expand its influence by offering security services through mercenary forces that profit from ongoing conflict. We conclude that arming host states is likely to prolong conflict, whereas negotiation and peace aid can isolate jihadist groups and promote a more stable peace.

items.title: Implementing A Public Health Approach to Preventing Violence Against Children
items.author: Ana FitzSimons
items.summary: This brief explores Brazil’s experience of implementing a public health approach to violence against children and adolescents, including the core elements as well as factors that are perceived to help and hinder implementation.
items.body:
Country Brief: Brazil

ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: End Violence Against Children Conference website (2026)

This brief explores Brazil’s experience of implementing a public health approach to violence against children and adolescents (VACA), including the core elements as well as factors that are perceived to help and hinder implementation. It analyses four key areas: 1) Policy & funding context; 2) Data & evidence; 3) Supporting the health sector; and 4) Multisector collaboration. The aim is to identify lessons to inform global progress in preventing VACA to 2030 and beyond. The brief draws on a desk review of relevant literature, data and legislation, as well as four interviews with key stakeholders, who were purposively sampled using the networks of the WHO and the brief’s authors.

items.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Use and Adolescent Mental Health
items.author: Jason M. Lavender
items.summary: This paper synthesizes recent literature on the relationships between GenAI use and adolescents’ mental health, with particular attention to problematic use and psychiatric vulnerabilities.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: Current Pediatrics Reports, Volume 14, Article Number 16 (2026). DOI: 10.1007/s40124-026-00388-8

To synthesize recent literature on the relationships between generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use and adolescents’ mental health, with particular attention to problematic use and psychiatric vulnerabilities.

Emerging evidence suggests associations between GenAI use and a range of adolescent mental health outcomes, including depression, anxiety, psychosis-related experiences, externalizing behaviors, eating disorder risk, and suicidality. Problematic patterns of use, including dependency and emotional reliance, may be particularly relevant among adolescents with preexisting psychiatric vulnerabilities. Current evidence suggests that these relationships may be bidirectional: psychological distress can motivate GenAI use for companionship, emotional support, or escape, while problematic use may reinforce maladaptive beliefs, displace real-world relationships, and amplify existing vulnerabilities. However, evidence remains predominantly cross-sectional, limiting causal inference.

GenAI may interact with and amplify underlying psychiatric vulnerabilities during adolescence, highlighting the importance of understanding patterns and motivations of use. Pediatricians and other clinicians caring for adolescents could consider not only the frequency of GenAI use but also motivations for use, problematic dependency, and socioemotional reliance. Identifying high-risk usage patterns of GenAI through longitudinal research, particularly among youth with preexisting psychiatric risks, may inform the development of tailored screening, intervention, and prevention strategies.

items.title: From Policy to Practice
items.author: Elizabeth D. Steiner
items.summary: We investigated the role that state policies related to preschool curriculum play in public school pre-K teachers’ reported curricula use across the United States.
items.body:
How State Policies Relate to Public Pre-K Teachers’ Curriculum Use

ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: National Institute for Early Education Research website (2026)

As many states expand the number of pre-K seats in public schools, policymakers are focused on better understanding the role of curriculum in ensuring high-quality early childhood education environments. By combining data from the National Institute for Early Education Research’s State of Preschool Yearbook with data from RAND's American Pre-K Teacher Survey, we investigated the role that state policies related to preschool curriculum play in public school pre-K teachers’ reported curricula use across the United States. We find substantial variation in the curricula teachers report using across states, and some differences across pre-K programs within states. In addition, specific state curriculum guidance appears to influence classroom curriculum use. When states required that teachers use specific curricula (rather than recommending curricula), teachers reported combining fewer curricula in their classrooms.

items.title: McChord Encourages Rider Mentorship Through Motorcycle Safety Program
items.author: SrA Benjamin Riddle
items.summary: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most.
items.body: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. Seven riders from multiple squadrons completed the course, including two members of the 142nd Wing, Oregon Air National Guard. The newly trained mentors will help expand local access to motorcycle safety training and assist experienced riders with mentoring others in their units. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most. “It comes down to what gets our guardians and our airmen injured, hurt, or killed,” said John McLaughlin, Air Force Safety Center deputy chief of traffic safety and outreach. “It’s the decision making, the behaviors that they’re using while they’re out on motorcycles.” McLaughlin highlighted how the program will be able to give units a more direct path to required training. “This training is a supplement to the current training and an alternative way of acquiring those skills across the DAF,” said McLaughlin. “This program will make it so here at JBLM, training can be done at the squadron level, and you don’t have to go all the way to the installation level to get training.” Before this new program, Air Force riders at JBLM would often need to coordinate through their motorcycle safety representatives, who would coordinate through wing safety who would then schedule training with the Army. The new mentor network will allow MSRs to provide instruction directly to the riders who need it. The course critically prepares mentors to lead discussions and practical exercises that reinforce riding fundamentals, sound judgment and risk management. The program also creates opportunities for riders to learn from one another’s experiences, said McLaughlin. “I can share stories to help others learn so they don’t have to go through some of the experiences I went through,” said McLaughlin. “That’s the main point of the program, current riders mentoring newer and older riders alike to all learn together.” Tech. Sgt. Corey Walrath, 62d Aircraft Maintenance Squadron squadron program manager, who helped bring McLaughlin to JBLM, said the local program gives the wing flexibility to meet increased demands for training. “With the rider mentor program, now Airmen can come to their MSRs or me for the 62d AMXS, and we can come up with a schedule that works for them right then and there,” said Walrath. “This will be able to quickly get them the training they need to stay safe on the roads.” Staff Sgt. Garrett Cofield, 62d Aerial Port Squadron passenger service supervisor, gave his thoughts on how the course reinforced the value of continuing to learn, regardless of experience level. “When I was doing the Level II, I thought I was a really good rider, I was a lot younger and I had a much bigger ego,” said Cofield. “I think coming to these trainings and learning the fundamentals and setting your ego aside is super important.” Ryan Meeks, 62d Airlift Wing occupational safety technician, took time to further highlight the critical nature of the program throughout the DAF. “Inexperienced riders are our primary concern as they account for 90% of the fatalities that the Airforce experiences,” said Meeks “Experienced riders can teach advanced riding techniques, but they also teach awareness, safety, temperament, and maturity factors. Having a trained and experienced rider mentor that you personally know or work with creates an environment of trust and familiarity that cannot be gained in a short class.” The continued growth of the program currently depends on experienced riders stepping forward to mentoring others and leading their unit is fundamental safety, said McLaughlin. If you are interested in becoming an MSR, rider mentor, or rider mentor instructor please contact the wing safety office today at 253-982-9999.
items.titleZh: 麦科德基地通过摩托车安全项目鼓励骑手导师带教
items.summaryZh: 2026年9月8日至9日，第62空运联队在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的Heritage Hill举办了空军部骑手导师项目教官课程。该项目支持强制性摩托车培训要求，即在取得一级初始驾照后一年内完成二级培训，此后每五年完成三级复训。该项目着重强调对骑手安全影响最大的各项决定。
items.zhFull: 第62空运联队于2026年9月8日至9日在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）的Heritage Hill主办了空军部骑手导师计划教官培训课程。来自多个中队的7名骑手完成了课程，其中包括俄勒冈州空军国民警卫队第142联队的2名成员。新受训的导师将帮助扩大当地获得摩托车安全培训的渠道，并协助经验丰富的骑手指导其所在单位的其他人。该计划支持强制性摩托车培训要求，即在获得I级初始驾照后一年内完成II级培训，此后每五年进行一次III级复训。该计划注重强调对骑手安全影响最大的决策。“归根结底，问题在于是什么导致我们的守护者和空军人员受伤、受到伤害或丧生，”空军安全中心交通安全与外联副主任约翰·麦克劳克林（John McLaughlin）说。“是决策，是他们在骑摩托车时所采取的行为。”麦克劳克林强调，该计划将能够为单位提供更直接的所需培训途径。“这项培训是对现有培训的补充，也是在整个空军部获得这些技能的另一种途径，”麦克劳克林说。“该计划将使得在JBLM这里，培训可以在中队一级完成，你不必一路到基地层级去接受培训。”在这项新计划之前，JBLM的空军骑手通常需要通过他们的摩托车安全代表进行协调，而摩托车安全代表则要通过联队安全部门协调，后者再与陆军安排培训。新的导师网络将使MSR能够直接向需要培训的骑手提供指导。该课程至关重要地培养导师引导讨论和实操练习的能力，以强化骑行基本功、正确判断和风险管理。麦克劳克林说，该计划还为骑手创造了从彼此经验中学习的机会。“我可以分享故事来帮助他人学习，这样他们就不必经历我经历过的一些事情，”麦克劳克林说。“这就是该计划的主旨：现有骑手指导新老骑手，让大家共同学习。”Tech. Sgt. 科里·沃尔拉斯（Corey Walrath），第62飞机维修中队项目主管，曾帮助将麦克劳克林请到JBLM，他说，当地计划使该联队能够灵活满足日益增长的培训需求。“有了骑手导师计划，现在空军人员可以来找他们的MSR，或者来找我（第62飞机维修中队），我们可以当场制定适合他们的安排，”沃尔拉斯说。“这样就能迅速让他们获得在道路上保持安全所需的培训。”Staff Sgt. 加勒特·科菲尔德（Garrett Cofield），第62空中港口中队旅客服务主管，谈到了该课程如何强化了无论经验水平如何都应继续学习的价值。“我参加II级培训时，以为自己是一名非常优秀的骑手，那时我年轻得多，也自负得多，”科菲尔德说。“我认为参加这些培训、学习基本功并放下自负非常重要。”瑞安·米克斯（Ryan Meeks），第62空运联队职业安全技术员，特意进一步强调该计划在整个空军部的关键性质。“经验不足的骑手是我们的首要关切，因为他们占空军所经历死亡事故的90%，”米克斯说。“经验丰富的骑手可以教授高级骑行技术，但他们也传授意识、安全、性情和成熟度等方面的因素。拥有一名你个人认识或共事过的、训练有素且经验丰富的骑手导师，会营造出一种信任和熟悉的氛围，这是短期课程无法获得的。”麦克劳克林说，该计划的持续发展目前取决于经验丰富的骑手挺身而出去指导他人，并带领其单位做好基本安全。如果你有兴趣成为MSR、骑手导师或骑手导师教官，请立即致电253-982-9999联系联队安全办公室。

items.title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft arrive at Creech AFB, advancing operational integration
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: The aircraft will undergo Air Combat Command-led operational experimentation to evaluate uncrewed systems and refine operational employment alongside crewed combat aircraft.
items.body:
Published Sept. 24, 2026

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

The Air Force received its first two Collaborative Combat Aircraft at Creech Air Force Base , Nevada, marking a significant step toward integrating uncrewed, semi-autonomous aircraft into future combat operations. Anduril delivered the first CCA, the YFQ-44A, to the Experimental Operations Unit last month, and General Atomics delivered the YFQ-42A last week. The aircraft will support Air Combat Command -led operational experimentation to refine how CCA will be employed alongside crewed aircraft in contested environments.

items.summaryZh: 该型飞机将接受空军作战司令部主导的作战试验，以评估无人系统，并完善其与有人作战飞机协同运用的方式。
items.zhFull:
发布于2026年9月24日

空军部长公共事务办公室

美国空军在位于内华达州的克里奇空军基地接收了首批两架协同作战飞机（CCA），这标志着在将无人、半自主飞机纳入未来作战行动方面迈出了重要一步。安杜里尔公司上个月向实验作战部队交付了首架 CCA——YFQ-44A，通用原子公司上周交付了 YFQ-42A。这些飞机将支持由空战司令部主导的作战实验，以完善 CCA 如何在对抗环境中与有人驾驶飞机协同运用。

items.title: Department of the Air Force pilot program expands to help more military spouses
items.author: Jennifer Gonzalez
items.summary: Administered by the AFPC and AFCS, the initiative connects active-duty spouses undergoing a permanent change of station with direct hiring opportunities.
items.body:
Published Sept. 23, 2026

By Jennifer Gonzalez

Air Force Personnel Center

A professional in her own right, Kayla Amie holds a master’s degree in organizational leadership and a Bachelor of Science in education, and has worked steadily since she was legally old enough to hold a job. But when she married a U.S. Air Force Airman, that professional background no longer guaranteed a career and steady income. “Every four years you are starting from scratch. I am ok with pivoting but it’s going from the fact that you worked so hard—being a professional—and having it taken away with each move and it not being your choice,” said Amie.

Luke AFB, Arizona

Goodfellow AFB, Texas

Laughlin AFB, Texas

Mountain Home AFB, Idaho

Travis AFB, California

Patrick SFB, Florida

Ramstein AB, Ramstein-Miesenbach

RAF Croughton, Northamptonshire

RAF Mildenhall, Suffolk

RAF Lakenheath, Suffolk

RAF Feltwell, Norfolk

Kadena AB, Okinawa

Only active-duty military spouses PCSing to the listed bases currently qualify to use the pilot program. Qualified spouses can enroll at any time into the GMSC Program using the Air Force Civilian Service website here .

发布于2026年9月23日

作者：珍妮弗·冈萨雷斯（Jennifer Gonzalez）

空军人事中心

凯拉·阿米（Kayla Amie）本身也是一位专业人士，拥有组织管理硕士学位和教育学专业理学学士学位，并且从达到法定就业年龄起就一直稳定工作。但当她嫁给一名美国空军军人后，那样的职业背景不再能保证她拥有职业生涯和稳定收入。“每四年你都要从头开始。我可以接受转型，但问题是，你如此努力——作为一名专业人士——而这一切却随着每一次搬迁被夺走，而且这不是你自己的选择，”阿米说。

items.title: DM Airmen participate in Coyote Storm 26.2 to reinforce AEW 2.0 concepts
items.author: Capt. M. Anna Turpin
items.summary: The multi-day training event operationalized Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concepts across cross-functional disciplines, including field medicine, combat search and rescue, and command and control.
items.body:
Published Sept. 22, 2026

By Capt. M. Anna Turpin

355th Wing Public Affairs

Airmen from the 355th Wing strengthened their ability to operate in contested environments during Coyote Storm 26.2 at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base , Sept. 14-17. Coyote Storm 26.2 was a training exercise focused on improving flexibility and readiness through the Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concept. AEW 2.0 training requires that preparation for deployments happens long before members go into theater and ensures that they have the time to train together across disciplines.

items.titleZh: DM空军人员参加“郊狼风暴26.2”演习，强化AEW 2.0概念
items.summaryZh: 这场为期多天的训练活动在多个跨职能领域落实了空中远征联队2.0概念，涵盖野战医疗、战斗搜救以及指挥控制。2026年9月17日，在亚利桑那州戴维斯-蒙森空军基地，一名美国空军战斗救援军官和第48救援中队的一名伞降救援兵在“郊狼风暴26.1”演习中练习装载演练。此次训练通过简化……强化了空中远征联队2.0这一优先事项。
items.zhFull:
发布于2026年9月22日

作者：Capt. M. Anna Turpin

第355联队公共事务办公室

9月14日至17日，第355联队的空军人员在戴维斯-蒙森空军基地举行的“郊狼风暴”26.2演习中，增强了在对抗环境中作战的能力。“郊狼风暴”26.2是一场训练演习，重点是通过“空中远征联队2.0”概念提高灵活性和战备水平。AEW 2.0训练要求，部署准备工作要远在人员进入战区之前就进行，并确保他们有时间跨专业一起训练。

items.body:
DAYTON, Ohio (AFLCMC) -- “You are part of the fight,” Lt. Gen. Jason Voorheis, commander of the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) told attendees at the Ohio Defense and Aerospace Forum earlier this week. “ General Dale White [Director, Critical Major Weapon Systems at the Pentagon] is fond of saying that militaries don't go to war - nations go to war. You all are part of what our nation brings to the fight in terms of developing fielding and getting capability into the hands of our warfighters.”

Voorheis spoke as part of a panel titled “Power Projection from the Heartland.” He was joined on stage by Brig. Gen. Timothy Helfrich, AFLCMC Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Fighters and Advanced Aircraft, alongside defense industry professionals TK Kubit and Anthony Cain. JP Nauseef of JobsOhio moderated the discussion. The forum was hosted by the Dayton Development Coalition.

Held at Wright State University on September 21, 2026, the forum highlighted the strategic alignment between Air Force modernization priorities and the Ohio defense ecosystem.

Acquisition Speed and Agility

The Ohio Defense Ecosystem

Workforce and Talent Development

In his opening remarks, Voorheis explained the Air Force acquisition workforce's shift to accept risk earlier, lean into commercial technology and open mission systems, and empower program teams to make decisions that drive projects forward.

Both Voorheis and Helfrich noted that acquisition teams at Wright-Patt and across the Center are transitioning away from platform-specific "stovepipes" to focus on broader, integrated capabilities across advanced aircraft. These teams are also balancing intensive current fleet modernization with future systems development by shifting from individual platform upgrades to an integrated, "system of systems" approach.

“I think one of the really important parts about the acquisition transformation is the change in philosophy and focus on delivering fielded capability as kind of the preeminent prioritized pacing thing that we do, and everything else is about how we achieve that to include the authorities we're giving PAEs,” noted Voorheis.

Helfrich’s Fighters and Advanced Aircraft portfolio includes the A-10, F-15, F-16, F-22, plus the FQ-42, FQ-44, other collaborative combat aircraft.

The Air Force Research Lab (AFRL) is also headquartered at Wright-Patt. Helfrich touted how AFRL led key advances in open architecture and credits AFRL with developing the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program.

“There would be no CCA without the Air Force Research Laboratory,” explained Helfrich. “Both the FQ-42 Vengeance [and] the FQ-44 Fury were heavily invested in by AFRL. Because software is sold separately with CCA, the mission autonomy work started at AFRL. They were really the ones who put together the first consortium to build Autonomous Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA). This has become a huge program, all made possible because of the investments by AFRL.”

For both Voorheis and Helfrich, the workforce and supporting infrastructure remain top concerns. Helfrich urged educators in the audience to modernize military engineering and software development classes. Both speakers noted the shortage of physical defense infrastructure in the area around Wright-Patterson, particularly for high-level classified work.

In addition to physical plant limitations, hiring remains a challenge. AFLCMC currently has over 1,700 vacancies , with more than half located at Wright-Patt. Most open positions are in technical fields like engineering and logistics. Business areas like contracting and program management also have many openings.

“We need help recruiting from the universities and from industry as well, both defense industry and non-defense industry,” explained Voorheis. “You don't have to come in with a lot of aerospace experience. What we really need is highly talented, motivated, critical thinkers.”

The panel marked the first time Lt. Gen. Voorheis has publicly spoken about his role leading AFLCMC since assuming command late last month .
items.titleZh: AFLCMC司令在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上阐述采办优先事项
items.summaryZh: 俄亥俄州代顿（AFLCMC）——“你们也是这场战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令Lt. Gen.贾森·沃希斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者表示。“Gen.戴尔·怀特（五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管）喜欢说，参战的不是军队——而是国家。你们所有人都是我们国家投入这场战斗的一部分，体现在研发、列装并把能力交到我们的……手中。”
items.zhFull:
代顿，俄亥俄州（AFLCMC）——“你们是战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令 Lt. Gen. 贾森·沃里斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者说。“戴尔·怀特将军（Dale White）[五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管]喜欢说，军队不会开战——国家才会开战。你们所有人都是我国为这场战斗所贡献力量的一部分，无论是开发、列装，还是把能力交到我们的作战人员手中。”

沃里斯作为题为“来自腹地的力量投射”的专题讨论小组成员发言。与他同台的有 Brig. Gen. 蒂莫西·赫尔弗里希（Timothy Helfrich），AFLCMC 战斗机与先进飞机组合采办执行官（PAE），以及国防工业专业人士 TK·库比特（TK Kubit）和安东尼·凯恩（Anthony Cain）。JobsOhio 的 JP·诺西夫（JP Nauseef）主持了讨论。该论坛由代顿发展联盟主办。

论坛于2026年9月21日在莱特州立大学举行，凸显了空军现代化优先事项与俄亥俄国防生态系统之间的战略协同。

采办速度与敏捷性

俄亥俄国防生态系统

劳动力与人才发展

沃里斯在开场致辞中解释说，空军采办队伍正在转变，更早接受风险，积极采用商业技术和开放任务系统，并赋予项目团队作出推动项目前进的决策的权力。

沃里斯和赫尔弗里希都指出，Wright-Patt 以及整个中心的采办团队正从针对特定平台的“烟囱式”模式转向，专注于先进飞机更广泛的一体化能力。这些团队还在平衡当前密集的机队现代化与未来系统开发，从单个平台升级转向一体化的“系统之系统”方法。

“我认为采办转型真正重要的部分之一，是理念的转变，以及把交付已列装能力作为我们最重要的优先事项和节奏牵引，而其他一切——包括我们赋予PAE的权限——都是为了实现这一目标，”沃海斯（Voorheis）指出。

赫尔弗里希（Helfrich）的“战斗机与先进飞机”组合包括A-10、F-15、F-16、F-22，以及FQ-42、FQ-44和其他协同作战飞机。

美国空军研究实验室（AFRL）也总部设在赖特-帕特森（Wright-Patt）。赫尔弗里希盛赞AFRL在开放架构方面引领了关键进展，并将协同作战飞机（CCA）项目的发展归功于AFRL。

“没有美国空军研究实验室，就不会有CCA，”赫尔弗里希解释道。“AFRL对FQ-42‘复仇’和FQ-44‘狂怒’都投入了大量资金。由于CCA的软件是单独销售的，任务自主性工作始于AFRL。他们确实是组建首个联盟来构建自主政府参考架构（A-GRA）的一方。这已成为一个庞大的项目，而这一切都得益于AFRL的投资。”

对沃海斯和赫尔弗里希而言，劳动力和配套基础设施仍是首要关切。赫尔弗里希敦促在场教育工作者对军事工程和软件开发课程进行现代化改革。两位发言人都指出，赖特-帕特森周边地区缺乏实体国防基础设施，尤其是用于高级别机密工作的设施。

除实体设施限制外，招聘仍是一项挑战。美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）目前有超过1,700个职位空缺，其中一半以上位于赖特-帕特森。大多数空缺职位属于工程和后勤等技术领域。合同签订和项目管理等业务领域也有许多空缺。

“我们需要在从大学以及产业界招聘方面获得帮助，既包括国防产业，也包括非国防产业，”沃海斯解释道。“你不需要带着丰富的航空航天经验入职。我们真正需要的是才华出众、积极进取、善于批判性思考的人。”

此次小组讨论标志着Lt. Gen.沃海斯自上月底就任指挥官以来，首次公开谈及他领导AFLCMC的职责。

Air Force Special Operations Command announced its small cruise missile, the AGM-190A Havoc Spear, has been evaluated in a test configuration and successfully meets requirements to become an available weapon system for broader real-world use across a variety of special operations and conventional aircraft.

items.body:
The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) has five unique ionizing radiation sources. All sources are maintained and operated by the Survivable Electronics Technology group (AFRL/RJSV) at Kirtland AFB, NM. These sources allow partnering researchers from industry, government labs, and universities to study a wide spectrum of total ionizing dose and prompt dose effects. The Survivable Electronics Technology group primarily uses these sources to determine the effects of radiation on advanced microelectronics, photonics, sensors, and micro-electromechanical systems needed for Air Force, Space Force, Department of Defense, and government space and missile systems .

Dosimetry; both CaF 2 and Ion Chambers

Fabricate test board and boxes for devices under test

Machine Shop access

B1500 w/ Switching Matrix

Mixed Signal Tester

Gamma Radiation Sources

The Cobalt-60 source can deliver a maximum total ionizing dose of ~20 krad (Si)/min to a minimum of <1 rad (Si)/min (which falls within ASTM 1019 specs of 300 to 50 rad(Si)/sec). Slightly higher dose rates may be attained if researchers are willing to accept that the source will appear as a line source opposed to a point source. This source produces two energy peaks at 1.17 and 1.33 MeV. The irradiator is a 360-degree panoramic irradiator, facility area is 1,500 ft 2 which provides the researcher the benefit of a large range of variable dose rates with plenty of area to conduct experiments. Evaluation of subsystems is possible in this cell. The large area of the facility minimizes the possibility of dose enhancement due to scatter. The high energy photons give a uniform dose deposition throughout the sample of interest. AFRL Co-60 facility provides the capability of performing in-situ experiments whereby measurements on components are taken during gamma irradiation through the use of 120 ft of BNC cables and CAT-5 cables that would allow the experimenters to control computer-controlled instrumentation from the control room to the irradiation test cell.

Total Dose Simulator

1.17 & 1.33 MeV Gammas

<.001 to 20 krad(Si)/min

1500 ft 2 of Test Cell

360-degree panoramic irradiator

The Cesium 137 low dose rate source will deliver a maximum of 40 rad(Si)/hr or a minimum of 0.3 rad(Si)/hr. This source produces gamma rays with a single energy peak at 662 keV. The Cs-137 source is capable of housing experiments which can fit in 1 ft 3 of volume. Due to the small exposure volume, a Pb/Al box is required for all experiments performed in this source to eliminate a dose enhancement effect. Will provide a Pb/Al box for experiments which meets ASTM standards if users do not have one. This source is capable of providing in-situ experimentation.

Low Total Dose Simulator

662 keV Gammas

0.005 to 0.667 rad(Si)/min

2.25 ft 2 Test Cell

X-Ray Radiation Sources

The ARACOR X-ray test system is used to investigate total ionizing dose effects on individual microelectronic devices. This system produces X-rays with energies that have a max range of 60 keV with peak energies at 10 keV and dose rates ranging from 0.1 to 30 krad (SiO 2 )/min. The system is capable to accommodating an 8” wafer for X-ray characterization of fabricated die or packaged devices with lids removed. Capable of utilizing a probe card to probe and bias up to 48 contacts concurrently.

10 to 60 keV spectrum, peak 10 keV

0.1 to 30 krad (SiO 2 )/min

Low Energy X-Ray (LEXR)

The Low Energy X-ray source is a Comet MXR-160/22 constant potential X-ray system which produces X-rays with energies that have a max range of 10 keV to 160 keV and peaks at 10 keV and 60 keV depending on the applied voltage. This source can produce a total ionizing dose rate of 360 krad (SiO 2 )/min. Exposure area is a 1.84 cm diameter at 10 cm from the X-ray tube. The distance from the tube can be varied up to 1 m to control dose rate. The X-ray tube current is variable in order to control dose rate, and the total energy deposited per unit area. This source is capable of providing in-situ experimentation.

High Total Dose Simulator

10 to 160 keV spectrum, peaks 10 and 60 keV(adjustable)

360 krad(SiO 2 )/min (max)

30 ft 2 Test Cell

Flash X-Ray (FXR)

The Flash X-ray source is a Febetron 705 machine which produces prompt dose exposures simulating nuclear weapons environments. This facility is capable of producing a 20 nanosecond pulse X-ray. The average 2.1 MeV of the X-rays produced in this facility provides a dose rate output from between 1x10 7 to 2x10 11 rad (Si)/sec. A 70 ft 2 . screen room is available for housing experiments in order to minimize the effects of EMP produced by the Febetron 705. To obtain higher dose rates, experiments may be performed in open air directly in front of the Febetron 705.

High Dose Simulator

X-ray Mode (Prompt dose)

1x10 7 to 2x10 11 rad(Si)/sec X-ray

items.title: AFRL demonstrates modular multimode propulsion system for sustained space maneuver
items.author: Patrick Londergan
items.summary: EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE, Calif. -- The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) recently demonstrated an innovative spacecraft propulsion system under realistic conditions in a specialized test facility at Edwards Air Force Base, California. “This work helps advance propulsion technologies that will give future space operators more flexible options for maneuver to adapt and sustain operations in demanding environments, as is required by U.S. Space Command,” said Dr. Andrew Williams , director of the
items.body:
EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE, Calif. -- The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) recently demonstrated an innovative spacecraft propulsion system under realistic conditions in a specialized test facility at Edwards Air Force Base, California.

“This work helps advance propulsion technologies that will give future space operators more flexible options for maneuver to adapt and sustain operations in demanding environments, as is required by U.S. Space Command,” said Dr. Andrew Williams , director of the AFRL Space Warfare Directorate .

Termed Propulsion Optimization UNifying Chemical and Electric (POUNCE), the demonstration proved the capability of an innovative propulsion technology called Modular Multimode Propulsion (MMP). MMP features both electric and chemical propulsion using the same propellant along with a single tank and feed system. Electric propulsion enables high-efficiency, low-thrust, long-duration and slow maneuvers; chemical propulsion enables shorter-duration, higher-thrust and faster maneuvers.

For the team behind POUNCE, the effort is not just about proving a concept—it is about giving future operators more flexible tools to meet mission demands in space.

“This demonstration is a pioneering leap in the advancement of flexible, modular and high-performance space propulsion technology to enable dynamic space operations,” said Dr. Javier Urzay, AFRL Rocket and Space Propulsion Division chief. “Our goal is to bring the future faster and deliver integrated capabilities for space warfare.”

The MMP architecture reduces system mass and volume, while increasing operational flexibility and resilience. It provides operators with discretion to allocate the same propellant to high-tempo maneuvers or more efficient repositioning of orbital assets.

The propellant used for the MMP system in this demonstration was the AFRL-developed Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic (ASCENT) fuel. AFRL has pursued several technology maturation activities jointly with industry to exploit the higher-density specific impulse and safer handling of ASCENT for spacecraft propulsion.

POUNCE’s MMP system also incorporated hardware from industry partners, including a composite conformal tank and propellant feed system from Flight Works, chemical thrusters from Igneon Aerospace, and a PALOMINO ion array electrospray thruster from Revolution Space.

“Alongside the relationships with our commercial partners, another equally important ingredient for this demonstration is the unique capabilities offered by the Space Propulsion Environment Facility (SPEF) at the AFRL Rocket Lab at Edwards AFB,” said Dr. Gregory Yandek, AFRL In-Space Propulsion Branch chief.

Inside SPEF, researchers were able to expose the experimental MMP system to the high-vacuum characteristics of orbital environments. Theorists first conceptualized the dual-mode combination of low-thrust and high-thrust propulsion capabilities for space missions in the 1960s, but experimentation with hardware has been limited to single-mode or primitive components until now.

Finally, the POUNCE MMP demonstration highlights how leveraging public-private partnerships can accelerate the transition of technology concepts toward operationally relevant capabilities. The demonstration hardware featured a highly modular design to quickly and easily swap different propulsion subsystems without having to change the parent system. This extra layer of flexibility will greatly increase system life replenishment and space maneuver capabilities in future operating environments.

The Air Force Research Laboratory is the Department of the Air Force’s primary scientific research and development center and one of six centers within Air Force Materiel Command. AFRL leads the discovery, development and delivery of technologies for air, space and multidomain. With a workforce spanning seven mission areas at more than 40 locations worldwide, AFRL conducts research ranging from basic science to advanced technology development. For more information, visit afresearchlab.com .

items.summaryZh: 加利福尼亚州爱德华兹空军基地——美国空军研究实验室（AFRL）近日在加利福尼亚州爱德华兹空军基地的一处专用试验设施中，在贴近真实的条件下演示了一款创新型航天器推进系统。“这项工作有助于推进推进技术的发展，从而为未来的太空操作人员提供更灵活的机动选择，使其能够在严苛环境中调整并持续开展行动，这也是美国太空司令部所要求的，”……主任安德鲁·威廉姆斯（Andrew Williams）博士表示。
